nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَتْ لأُخْتِهِ قُصِّيهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, follow his track.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: that is, trace his track and seek him.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ عَن جُنُبٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, from afar; and from it comes al-ajnabī (the stranger). The poet said:
قلا تَحْرِمَنِّي نَائِلاً عَنْ جَنَابةٍ * فإنّي امْرُؤٌ وَسْطَ القِباَبِ غرِيبٌ
(So do not deny me a gift out of estrangement, for I am a man who is a stranger among the tents.)
[Translator's note: the verse opens «قلا» in the source, apparently for «فلا»; it is reproduced as written.]
The meaning is: she watched him from afar so that they would not become aware of her.
Abū ʿAmr said: Some of the commentators said: ﴿فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ عَنْ جُنُبٍ﴾ means out of longing. He said: and it is a dialect of Judhām; they say جَنَبْتُ إلى لقائِكَ, meaning "I longed to meet you".
Then He said: ﴿وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾, that is, they were not aware that she was his sister.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
That is, before his return to his mother.
Qatāda said: He would not accept any breast, so his sister said: ﴿هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُ نَاصِحُونَ﴾?
Al-Suddī said: They grew suspicious of her when she said to them ﴿وَهُمْ لَهُ نَاصِحُونَ﴾, so she said: I only meant "and they are sincere towards the king". Then she directed them to his mother, and they called her to him so that she might nurse him for them at their expense.
That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَرَدَدْنَاهُ إلَى أُمِّهِ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلاَ تَحْزنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّا رَادُّوهُ إلَيْكِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَٱسْتَوَىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said, from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda: ﴿لَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَٱسْتَوَىٰ﴾ means thirty-three years, and ﴿واسْتَوى﴾ means he reached forty years.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh holds that the singular of "الأشُدِّ" is شِدَّةٌ.
Al-Kisāʾī and some of the Basrans said: the singular is شَدٌّ.
Abū ʿUbayda said: it has no singular.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, [﴿آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْماً﴾: he said: understanding (fiqh) and intellect.
﴿وَعِلْمَاً﴾ means prophethood.]

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Qatāda said: at the time of midday, while the people were asleep.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلاَنِ هَـٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِ وَهَـٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ﴾.
Abū Mālik said: one of them was from the Children of Israel and the other was a Copt.
Abū Jaʿfar said: If it is asked: how is ﴿هَذَا﴾ (this) said of someone absent?
The answer is that the meaning is: the onlooker, when he looked at the two of them, would say: this one is of his faction, and this one is of his enemy.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱسْتَغَاثَهُ ٱلَّذِي مِن شِيعَتِهِ عَلَى ٱلَّذِي مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ فَوَكَزَهُ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
﴿فَٱسْتَغَاثَهُ ٱلَّذِي مِن شِيعَتِهِ﴾ means the Israelite, ﴿عَلَى ٱلَّذِي مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ﴾ means the Copt.
﴿فَوَكَزَهُ مُوسَىٰ﴾ means the Copt.
Mujāhid said: he struck him with his clenched fist.
And so it is in the language; it is said وَكَزَه when he struck him with his clenched fist on his chest.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is ﴿فَنَكَزَهُ مُوسَى﴾, and the meaning is the same; likewise لَكَمَهُ, لكَزَهُ and لَهَزَهُ.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: he struck him with the staff. ﴿فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ﴾ means he killed him. ﴿قَالَ هَـٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾: this shows that his killing him was by mistake, and that he had not been commanded to kill or to fight.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيراً لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾.
That is, a helper to the criminals.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He did not make an exception [by saying "if Allah wills"], so he was put to the test.
That is, he was tested in that the Israelite became the cause of what he had done being reported.
Al-Kisāʾī said: ﴿فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيراً لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾
carries the meaning of a supplication.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ﴿فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي ظَهِيراً لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَصْبَحَ فِي ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفاً يَتَرَقَّبُ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, he was watching out for pursuit. ﴿فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي ٱسْتَنْصَرَهُ بِٱلأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُ﴾, that is, he was calling on him for help against another man. ﴿قَالَ لَهُ مُوسَىٰ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِيٌّ مُّبِينٌ﴾, because he had been the cause of the killing.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِي هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
a- The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū Mālik is that the meaning is: when Moses wanted to seize the Copt, the Israelite imagined that Moses ﷺ [meant] to seize him, because he had spoken harshly to him; so the Israelite said: ﴿يٰمُوسَىٰ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِي﴾. The Copt heard the words, and went and divulged the matter against Moses.
b- It has also been said that the meaning is: when the Israelite wanted Moses to seize the one who was an enemy to them both.
It is related from Ibn Najīḥ: when the Israelite wanted to seize the Copt, Moses, peace be upon him, forbade him, and the Israelite became afraid of him and said: ﴿أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِي﴾ (the verse), and so the Copt informed against him.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: he was the believer of Pharaoh's family.
﴿قَالَ يٰمُوسَىٰ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿يَأْتَمِرُونَ﴾ means they are consulting one another, and he recited:
أَحَارُ بنَ عَمْرِوٍ كَأَنِّي خَمِرٌ * وَيَعْدُو عَلَى المَرْءِ ما يَأْتَمِرْ
(O Ḥārith son of ʿAmr, it is as if I am dazed, and what a man plots turns against him.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is a mistake. If it were as he said, it would be "يتآمرونَ فِيكَ", that is, they consult about you, meaning they seek one another's counsel.
Rather the meaning of ﴿يَأْتَمِرُونَ﴾ is: they are intending (yahummūna), from His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وائْتَمِرُوا بينكُمْ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾. Likewise the meaning of:
"وَيْعُدو عَلَى المَرْءِ مَا يَأْتَمِرُ" (what a man intends turns against him)
is as it is said: whoever widens a pit falls into it.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: that is, towards Madyan.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّيۤ أَن يَهْدِيَنِي سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, the road to Madyan.
Abū Mālik said: Pharaoh sent people after him and said to them: Seek him in the side-paths, for Moses does not know the road. Then an angel came riding a horse and carrying a short spear (ʿanaza), and said to Moses: Follow me. So he followed him and he guided him to the road.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ﴾.
That is, a company.
﴿وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَينِ تَذُودَانِ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ودونَهُمُ امرأتانِ حَابِسَتانِ" (and apart from them two women holding back). He asked them why they were holding back, and they said: We are not strong enough to water [our flock] along with the people, until they go away.
The meaning of ﴿تَذُودَانِ﴾ — according to what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās — is: they were holding back.
Sufyān ibn Abī al-Haytham related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿تَذُودَانِ﴾, he said: holding back.
Hushaym related from Ḥuṣayn from Abū Mālik: ﴿وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَينِ تَذُودَانِ﴾, he said: they were holding back their sheep until the people had finished, so that the well would be free for them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear view. It is said ذَادَ، يَذُودُ [when one holds back].
And ذُدْتُ الشيءَ means: I held the thing back. Then the object is omitted, either to leave it vague for the one addressed or because his knowledge of it makes it unnecessary.
The view of Qatāda is that they were keeping the people away from their sheep.
The first is more fitting, because after it comes ﴿قَالَتَا لاَ نَسْقِي حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ﴾.
Had they been keeping the people away from their sheep, they would not have given the reason for delaying their watering until the shepherds went away.
﴿قَالَ مَا خَطْبكُمَا﴾? That is, what is your situation and what is your affair? ﴿قَالَتَا لاَ نَسْقِي حَتَّىٰ يَصْدُرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ﴾.
Whoever reads ﴿يُصْدِرَ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ has omitted the object, that is, until they drive their sheep away.
﴿وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾: the point of this is that he is unable to do the watering because of his old age; "that is why we have come out, though we are women".

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ﴾.
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said: "When the shepherds had drawn water, they covered the well with a rock that only ten men could lift. Moses ﷺ came and wrenched it off, and drew a single bucket (dhanūb), needing no other, and watered for the two of them."
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ﴾.
ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He asked for nothing but food.
Mujāhid said: He had nothing to eat.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَاهُمَا تَمْشِي عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ﴾.
The meaning is: the two of them went to their father before their usual time and told him about Moses and his watering; so he sent one of them, and she came walking with shyness.
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said: She walked with her hand over her face out of modesty; she was not a bold woman (salfaʿ), one who goes out and comes in freely.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ﴾.
That is, he told him his story and informed him of his killing the soul and of his fear. ﴿قَالَ لاَ تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾, because "Madyan" was not in Pharaoh's dominion.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا يٰأَبَتِ ٱسْتَأْجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَأْجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِيُّ ٱلأَمِينُ﴾.
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn related from ʿUmar, who said: He said to her: How did you come to know his strength and his trustworthiness?
She said: As for his strength, he lifted a stone that only ten can carry.
As for his trustworthiness, when he came with me I walked in front of him, and he said to me: Walk behind me and direct me along the road, lest the wind outline you to me.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنِّيۤ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ٱبْنَتَيَّ هَاتَيْنِ﴾.
In a report it is said that he married him to the younger one, whose name was "Ṭūriyā".
Then He said: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَن تَأْجُرَنِي ثَمَانِيَ حِجَجٍ﴾, that is, that you be a hired man for me. ﴿فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْراً فَمِنْ عِندِكَ﴾, that is, that will be a favour from you. ﴿قَالَ ذَلِكَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكِ﴾, that is, you have what you stipulated and I have the like of it. ﴿أَيَّمَا الأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلاَ عُدْوَانَ عَلَيَّ﴾: al-ʿudwān is overstepping in wrongdoing.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهْلِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān related from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "I asked Gabriel which of the two terms Moses fulfilled, and he said: The more complete and the more perfect of the two."
The meaning of ﴿لَّعَلِّيۤ آتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ﴾ is: perhaps I will learn why it has been kindled.
﴿أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
Qatāda said: al-jadhwa is the stump of a tree with fire in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Likewise al-judhwa, with ḍamma, kasra and fatḥa on the jīm; and al-jidhwa is a large piece of wood with fire in it but no flame.
And He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿في البُقْعَةِ المُبَارَكَةِ من الشَّجَرَة﴾, because He, Mighty and Majestic is He, spoke to him there.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوۤءٍ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿أُسْلُكْ﴾ is: insert.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-janāḥ (the wing) here is the staff.
No one among the people of exegesis said this, nor anyone among the early authorities that I know of. Most of the lexicographers report that al-janāḥ is from the lower part of the upper arm to the end of the armpit, and sometimes the hand is called janāḥ; for this reason Abū ʿUbayda said:
﴿جَنَاحَكَ﴾ means your hand.
Mujāhid said: ﴿مِنَ الرَّهْبِ﴾ means from fear.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَذَانِكَ بُرْهَانَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: meaning the hand and the staff.
And al-burhān is the proof.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿جَنَاحَكَ﴾ means your hand.
Abū Zayd said: the upper arm (al-ʿaḍud) is the janāḥ. Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʿath informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, from his father, from Bishr ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ﴾, that is, put your hand in and place it on your chest until the terror leaves you.
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: There is no one after Moses who is seized by terror and then puts his hand in and places it on his chest, but that the terror leaves him.

nahhas-meani:34-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَرْسِلْهِ مَعِيَ رِدْءاً يُصَدِّقُنِي﴾.
Al-ridʾ is help; and أَرْدَأه and رَدَأه mean: he helped him.
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ﴾.
That is, We will help you and strengthen you. It is a figure of speech, because the strength of the hand lies in the upper arm. ﴿وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَاناً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: that is, a proof.
﴿فَلاَ يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِآيَاتِنَآ﴾.
[That is, you two will be protected by Our signs.]
It is also possible that the meaning is: and We will give you both authority by Our signs — that is, by the staff and the hand — and what resembles them.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَوْقِدْ لِي يٰهَامَانُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: until it becomes baked brick.
Qatāda said: It has reached me that he was the first to make baked brick.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَٱجْعَل لِّي صَرْحاً﴾.
It has been said: a lofty building.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ مِن بَعْدِ مَآ أَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْقُرُونَ ٱلأُولَىٰ بَصَآئِرَ﴾.
That is, a clarification.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلْغَرْبِيِّ إِذْ قَضَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلأَمْرَ﴾.
Qatāda said: it is a mountain.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كُنتَ ثَاوِياً﴾, that is, residing.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ إِذْ نَادَيْنَا﴾.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq related from al-Thawrī, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAlī ibn Mudrik, from Abū Zurʿa ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr — who traced the report back [to the Prophet] — concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ إِذْ نَادَيْنَا﴾: he said: They were called: O community of Muḥammad, I answered you before you called upon Me, and I gave to you before you asked Me. That is His saying ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ إِذْ نَادَيْنَا﴾.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن رَّحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾.
That is, you did not witness the stories of the prophets, nor were they recited to you; but We sent you and revealed them to you as a mercy, so that you might warn a people and make known to them the destruction of those who were destroyed and the success of those who succeeded, that perhaps they might remember.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْلاۤ أَن تُصِيبَهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
That is, were it not for this, We would not have needed to send messengers and to present proof after proof.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِنْ عِندِنَا﴾.
That is, the manifest, clear proofs, whose delay they might otherwise have used as an argument. ﴿قَالُواْ لَوْلاۤ أُوتِيَ مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ﴾, meaning the staff, the parting of the sea and the like.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: The Jews told Quraysh to ask Muḥammad ﷺ for the like of what Moses was given. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said to Muḥammad ﷺ: Tell them to say to them: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ﴾?
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ سَاحِرَانِ تَظَاهَرَا﴾.
Sufyān related from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: ﴿قَالُوا سَاحِرَانِ تَظَاهَرَا﴾, he said: Moses and Aaron, may Allah bless them both.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: they mean Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them both.
Shuʿba related from Abū Ḥamza from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿قَالُوا سَاحِرَانِ تَظَاهَرَا﴾, he said: Moses and Muḥammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace.
Shuʿba likewise related it from Abū Jamra from Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḥasan said the same.
ʿIkrima, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī and Abū Razīn read it as ﴿قَالُوا سِحْرَانِ تَظَاهَرَا﴾.
ʿIkrima said: meaning two books.
Abū Razīn said: meaning the Torah and the Gospel.
Al-Farrāʾ said: meaning the Torah and the Qurʾan.
Some of those who read this reading argue from His saying: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوْا بِكِتَابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ هُوَ أَهْدَى مِنْهُمَا أَتَّبِعْهُ﴾.
The meaning according to the first reading is: it is better guidance than the books of the two of them.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ وَصَّلْنَا لَهُمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾.
That is, We made part of it follow upon another.
Mujāhid said: meaning for Quraysh.
Al-Ḥasan read ﴿وَصَلْنَا﴾ without doubling (takhfīf).

nahhas-meani:53-53.t: The meaning of ﴿إنَّا كُنَّا مِنْ قَبْلِهِ مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ is that they found the description of the Prophet ﷺ in their scripture before he was sent, so they believed in him, and then they believed in him after he was sent.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُؤْتُونَ أَجْرَهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ﴾.
The meaning may be: before the Prophet ﷺ; or it may be: before the Qurʾan.
The meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ﴾
is: they repel, by their deeds of good, the evil deeds that they had done.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا سَمِعُواْ ٱللَّغْوَ أَعْرَضُواْ عَنْهُ﴾.
That is, what is not permissible and what ought to be discarded.
Mujāhid said: These were people of the People of the Book who embraced Islam, and the idolaters used to harm them.
The meaning of ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ is: we have parted from you; it has nothing to do with greeting, and this is a usage well known among the Arabs.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّكَ لاَ تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī related from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from his father, who said: Abū Jahl ibn Hishām and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayya ibn al-Mughīra came to "Abū Ṭālib" during the illness in which he died, and the Prophet ﷺ came and said: O uncle, say "There is no god but Allah", a word by which I may plead for you before Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Abū Jahl said to him: O Abū Ṭālib, would you turn away from the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib!? The last thing he said to them was: He is upon the creed of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. The Prophet ﷺ said: I will not stop asking forgiveness for you.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿إِنَّكَ لاَ تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ﴾.
And there was revealed concerning him: ﴿مَا كَان لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا أُولي قُرْبَى﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ﴾ may be: whom you wish to guide.
Or the meaning may be: whom you love because of his kinship.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَن يَشَآءُ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾.
[That is, Allah knows best who deserves guidance from among those who deserve error, and to Allah belongs perfect wisdom.]

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُوۤاْ إِن نَّتَّبِعِ ٱلْهُدَىٰ مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفْ مِنْ أَرْضِنَآ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: This is the saying of the idolaters who were in Mecca.
Someone else said: They said to the Prophet ﷺ: We know that what you have brought is the truth, but we dislike following you, lest we be targeted and snatched away for opposing the people.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَماً آمِناً﴾.
That is, they were secure before Islam; had they embraced Islam they would have been more firmly secure.
Qatāda said: The people of the Sanctuary were secure; one of them would go out, and if he was accosted he would say: I am one of the people of the Sanctuary, and he would be left alone, while others would be killed and plundered.
Mujāhid said from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿يُجْبَىٰ إِلَيْهِ ثَمَرَاتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾,
that is, the fruits of the lands.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا﴾.
Al-baṭar is insolence in prosperity.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is: it was insolent in its livelihood.
Al-Farrāʾ said: its livelihood made it insolent.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَتِلْكَ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ لَمْ تُسْكَن مِّن بَعْدِهِمْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is that they fell into ruin, so only a little of them was inhabited, and the rest is ruins.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يَبْعَثَ فِيۤ أُمِّهَا رَسُولاً﴾.
That is, in the greatest of them; and the Mother of Towns (umm al-qurā) is Mecca.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن وَعَدْنَاهُ وَعْداً حَسَناً فَهُوَ لاَقِيهِ كَمَن مَّتَّعْنَاهُ مَتَاعَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
By it is meant the believer and the unbeliever.
It has also been said: it was revealed concerning the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Jahl.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, the people of the Fire, they have been brought forward.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنَادِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكَآئِيَ﴾.
That is, and on the day Allah calls mankind: ﴿أَيْنَ شُرَكَآئِيَ﴾? That is, according to your claim.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ رَبَّنَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أَغْوَيْنَآ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾ means the devils.
Someone else said: ﴿حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾ means the proof was established against them, so they were punished.
﴿رَبَّنَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أَغْوَيْنَآ﴾, that is, we called them to error.
﴿أَغْوَيْنَاهُمْ كَمَا غَوَيْنَا﴾, that is, we led them astray as we went astray.
﴿تَبَرَّأْنَآ إِلَيْكَ مَا كَانُوۤاْ إِيَّانَا يَعْبُدُونَ﴾: so they disowned one another and became enemies, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿الأَخِلاَّءُ يَوْمِئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إلاَّ المُتَّقِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ لَهُمْ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلْعَذَابَ لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾.
That is, they called them, but they did not answer them with any argument.
﴿وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلْعَذَابَ لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾: the apodosis (jawāb) of "لَوْ" is omitted, that is: had they been guided, they would not have called them.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلأَنبَـآءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَهُمْ لاَ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿ٱلأَنبَـآءُ﴾ are the arguments.
﴿فَهُمْ لاَ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ﴾, he said: by their lineages.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيَخْتَارُ﴾.
This is a complete stop (al-tamām).
That is, and He chooses the messengers.
﴿مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ ٱلْخِيَرَةُ﴾.
That is, those whom they chose are not messengers.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلنَّهَارَ سَرْمَداً إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿سَرْمَدَاً﴾ means perpetual.
﴿مَنْ إلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِضِيَاءٍ﴾, that is, with daytime in which you earn your living, and which makes your fruits and crops thrive.
[Translator's note: the source reads ﴿ٱلنَّهَارَ﴾ (the day) in the verse quoted here and «بنَهارٍ» in the gloss, although the wording ﴿بِضِيَاءٍ﴾ belongs to verse 71, which speaks of the night; it is translated as written.]

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن رَّحْمَتِهِ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسْكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبتَغُواْ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them is that the meaning is: that you may rest in the night, and that you may seek of His bounty in the day.
The other view is that the meaning is: that you may rest in both of them; and He said "فيه" (in it, singular) because night and day are light and darkness, as you say with maṣdars (verbal nouns): ذهابُك ومجيئُك يؤذيني ("your going and your coming annoys me", with a singular verb).
So the meaning would be: He made time for you, that you may rest in it and that you may seek of His bounty.
The first view is better known in the speech of the Arabs: they mention two items and then gather their explanations together, when the listener knows which belongs to which.
As it is related from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba that he said: "How fine are good deeds following upon bad deeds, and how ugly are bad deeds following upon good deeds! And finer than this, and uglier than that, are bad deeds upon bad deeds and good deeds upon good deeds."
Abū Jaʿfar said: So he gave the explanation collectively, and this is eloquent and frequent.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً فَقُلْنَا هَاتُواْ بُرْهَانَكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿شَهِيداً﴾ means a prophet.
﴿فَقُلْنَا هَاتُواْ بُرْهَانَكُمْ﴾, he said: that is, your proof for what you used to say and do.
﴿فَعَلِمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱلْحَقَّ لِلَّهِ﴾, that is, that Allah is One and that the truth is what the prophets brought.
﴿وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾, that is, they did not benefit from what they worshipped besides Allah; rather it harmed them.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ قَارُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: He was his paternal cousin.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
That is, he overstepped the bounds in opposing Moses ﷺ and in denying him.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوءُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلْقُوَّةِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash related from Khaythama, who said: His keys were made of leather, each key the size of a finger, for a treasury; sixty mules carried them when he rode out.
Mujāhid said: They were of camel hide.
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: Forty mules carried them.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: The keys of Qārūn were carried by forty men.
Ibn ʿUyayna said: ﴿ٱلْعُصْبَةِ﴾ is forty men.
Mujāhid said: ﴿ٱلْعُصْبَةِ﴾ is from ten to fifteen.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-ʿuṣba in the language is the group whose members band together in support of one another.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿لَتَنُوءُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ﴾: its interpretation is that the band would be weighed down by them, as [the poet] said:
* "وتَشْقَى الرِّمَاحُ بِالضَّيَاطِرَة الحُمْرِ" *
(and the spears are made wretched by the ruddy ḍayāṭira)
Al-ḍayāṭira are followers and hirelings.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda holds that this is an inversion (maqlūb), and this is a mistake. What is correct in it is what Abū Zayd said: it is said نُؤْتُ بالحِمْلِ when you rise with the load with difficulty, and نَاءَنِي and أَنَاءَني when it weighed me down.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: al-Aṣmaʿī was asked about the poet's word "وتشقى", and he said: Yes, they are made wretched by the men.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ لاَ تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْفَرِحِينَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿ٱلْفَرِحِينَ﴾ are the insolent, who do not thank Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, for what He has given them.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: His share of this world is acting in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, for which he will be rewarded on the Day of Resurrection.
Ashʿath related from al-Ḥasan, who said: Keep back what sustains you, and send ahead what is surplus.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: Seek what is lawful.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Mujāhid is very good, because a person's real share in this world is that which brings him to Paradise.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلاَ تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾, he says: Do not neglect to work for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in this world.
It has also been said: and do not forget to give thanks for your share.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِيۤ﴾.
It is related that "Qārūn" was one of the reciters of the Torah among the Children of Israel.
The meaning is: I was only given it on account of knowledge, as I see it.
As for what is related, that he practised alchemy, it is not sound.
It has also been said that the meaning is: on account of knowledge of the ways by which wealth is earned — and he abandoned thankfulness.
Ibn Zayd said: He — that is, Qārūn — said: Were it not that Allah is pleased with me and knows my merit, He would not have given me this.
This is the most fitting of them; what comes after it points to it.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يُسْأَلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يُعْرَف المُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾:
blue-eyed, with black faces; the angels do not ask about them, because they recognise them.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَلاَ يُسْأَلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ means they enter the Fire without reckoning.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: ﴿وَلاَ يُسْأَلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ means the later one does not ask why the earlier one perished, so as to take warning.
It has also been said: they are not asked about them with a question seeking information.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ فِي زِينَتِهِ﴾.
ʿUthmān ibn al-Aswad related from Mujāhid, who said: He and his companions came out on white work-horses (barādhīn) bearing saddles of purple, and they were wearing safflower-dyed garments.
Qatāda said: They came out on four thousand mounts bearing red cloths, among them a thousand white mules bearing red velvet covers.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يُلَقَّاهَآ إِلاَّ ٱلصَّابِرُونَ﴾.
That is, none is granted this deed — namely the saying ﴿ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِّمَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً﴾ — except the patient.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَخَسَفْنَا بِهِ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was swallowed down to the lowest earth.
﴿فَمَا كَانَ لَهُ مِن فِئَةٍ﴾, that is, any party.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ وَأَصْبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوْاْ مَكَانَهُ بِٱلأَمْسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيْكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ﴾.
His saying ﴿وَيْكَأَنَّ﴾: it has been said that it is "وَيْكَ أنَّ", and that "يْكَ" means وَيْلُكَ (woe to you).
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is not sound, because this lām is not dropped; and if it were so, it would have to be said: ويْلَكَ إِنَّه.
Nor is it permissible to supply an implied "إعْلَمْ" (know), since there is no address to a single person here.
What is correct in this is what al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī said.
Al-Kisāʾī said: "وَيْ" here is a connective (ṣila), and carries the meaning of wonder.
Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَيْكَأَنَّهُ لاَ يُفْلِحُ الكَافِرُونَ﴾ and His saying ﴿وَيْكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾, and he held that it is "ويْ" separated from "كَأَنَّ".
And the meaning falls on this: that the people became alert and spoke according to the extent of their knowledge,
or they were alerted, and it was said to them: Does it not seem to you that this is so? And Allah knows best.
As for the commentators, they said its meaning is: Have you not seen that Allah…
Qatāda said: ﴿وَيْكَأَنَّ﴾: the meaning is: Do you not know?
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of al-Khalīl agrees with this, and the lexicographers recited:
ويْ كَأَنْ مَنْ يَكُنْ لَهُ نَشَبٌ * يُحْبَبْ ومن يَفْتَقِرْ يَعِشْ عَيْشَ ضُرِّ
(Ah, it seems that whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.)
It is written joined in the Muṣḥaf, as though, since they used it so often, they made it together with what follows into a single thing.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تِلْكَ ٱلدَّارُ ٱلآخِرَةُ نَجْعَلُهَا لِلَّذِينَ لاَ يُرِيدُونَ عُلُوّاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ فَسَاداً﴾.
Sufyān related from Manṣūr from Muslim al-Baṭīn, who said: al-ʿuluww (exaltation) is arrogance without right, and al-fasād (corruption) is taking wealth without right.
Al-Thawrī said: ﴿وَلاَ فَسَادَاً﴾ means acts of disobedience.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِي فَرَضَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ لَرَآدُّكَ إِلَىٰ مَعَادٍ﴾.
ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿إِلَىٰ مَعَادٍ﴾ means to Mecca.
Yūnus ibn Isḥāq likewise related it from Mujāhid.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: to death.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: until He brings you to life on the Day of Resurrection.
Al-Zuhrī and al-Ḥasan said: «المَعَادُ» is the Day of Resurrection.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is well known in the language; it is said: "between me and you is al-maʿād", that is, the Day of Resurrection, because people return (yaʿūdūna) on it alive.
The first view is good and frequent, and Allah knows best what He intended.
The meaning would then be: He who sent down the Qurʾan upon you — when you did not expect it to be cast to you — will surely return you to a place of return, that is, to your homeland and place of return, meaning Mecca. And it is said: so-and-so returned to his maʿād, that is, to his home.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلاَّ وَجْهَهُ﴾.
Sufyān said: that is, except what is done seeking His Face.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-Thawrī narrated to me, saying: I asked Abū ʿUbayda about His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلاَّ وَجْهَهُ﴾, and he said: except His standing (jāh), as you say: so-and-so has a "face" among people, meaning standing.
It has also been said: ﴿إِلاَّ وَجْهَهُ﴾ means except Him, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And you say: "May Allah honour his face", and "so-and-so is the face of the people".
The view of Sufyān is well known in the language: that is, everything the servants do perishes except the aspect (wajh) by which they turn towards Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿طسۤمۤ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿ طسۤمۤ﴾ is one of the names of the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ﴾.
i.e. whose blessing and goodness are manifest, and which makes clear truth from falsehood, the lawful from the unlawful, the stories of the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, and the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ.
And one says: أَبَانَ الشَّيءُ, بَانَ and أَبَانَ [Translator's note: أبان is repeated in the source]: it became clear.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿نَتْلُواْ عَلَيْكَ مِن نَّبَإِ مُوسَىٰ وَفِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
Al-nabaʾ is the news.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلاَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Al-Suddī said: i.e. he behaved as a tyrant.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. he divided them.
Al-Suddī said: i.e. he divided them among the filthy (menial) tasks.
Qatāda said: ﴿شِيَعَاً﴾ i.e. he slaughtered some of them, let some of them live, and killed some of them.
And al-shiyaʿ according to the lexicographers is the plural of shīʿa, and al-shīʿa is the faction whose members help and support one another.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتُضْعِفُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Meaning the Children of Israel, may Allah bless him; ﴿وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةً﴾ i.e. rulers; ﴿وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ ٱلْوَارِثِينَ﴾ i.e. the inheritors of Pharaoh and his chiefs.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنْهُمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يَحْذَرونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: Pharaoh had a ḥāzī — and the ḥāzī is the astrologer — who said to him: A child will be born this year who will take away your kingdom. So Pharaoh ordered the killing of the newborn boys in that year. He said: That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَنُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنْهُمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يَحْذَرونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي ٱليَمِّ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: He cast it into her soul.
And it was said: It was a dream that she saw.
Someone else said: Rather it was a guarantee from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Revelation (al-waḥy) in the language is informing in secret; therefore it is permissible to call inspiration waḥy, as He, the Exalted, said ﴿وَأَوْحَى ربُّكَ إلى النَّحلِ﴾, and He said ﴿وإذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوَارِيِّينَ﴾.
And the third statement — its soundness is indicated by His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ﴾ and His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْد اللَّهِ حقٌّ﴾.
And al-yamm is the sea.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً﴾.
Since their picking him up led to this, it was said: they picked him up for it; just as it is said of someone who earned his wealth and it ruined him: he only earned it so that it would destroy him. This is the school of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh and of those grammarians whose opinion is approved, and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ لِّي وَلَكَ﴾.
This is the end of the statement (a complete pause). The evidence for that is that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ لِّي وَلَكَ﴾. [Translator's note: the quoted reading of Ibn Masʿūd is identical to the standard text in the source; the variant attributed to him elsewhere is «… لِي وَلَكَ لا تَقْتُلُوهُ», with «لا تقتلوه» placed before «قرة عين», which is what would support the pause.]
The meaning of ﴿قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ﴾ is: his eye was cooled (qarrat), from al-qurr, which is cold, i.e. it was not heated by weeping.
And it was said: qarrat is from قَرَّ في المكان (he settled in the place), i.e. it did not weep.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَارِغاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are four statements on it:
a- Among them is what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barāthī narrated to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, from Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, about His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَارِغاً﴾: he said: It became empty of everything in this world except the remembrance of Mūsā ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū ʿUbayda, Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said likewise.
b- Al-Kisāʾī said: ﴿فَارِغاً﴾ i.e. forgetful and distracted, as it is said of one whose need was not met: faragha, and of the dead: he has faragha (finished).
And al-Kisāʾī rejected that the meaning is: empty of everything except the remembrance of Mūsā, (saying) the meaning is not that.
c- Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: ﴿وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَارِغاً﴾ — (empty) of the revelation; ﴿إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ﴾ i.e. (disclose) the revelation.
d- Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَارِغاً﴾ i.e. (free) of grief, when she learnt that he had not drowned.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The soundest of these statements is the first, and those who said it are more knowledgeable about the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If it was empty of everything except the remembrance of Mūsā, then it was empty of the revelation (too). And their saying "the dead man has finished with this" means: he has finished with what was incumbent on him to do.
And the statement of Abū ʿUbayda — "empty of sorrow" — is an ugly mistake, because after it comes ﴿إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ لَوْلاۤ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا﴾. [Translator's note: in item a- Abū ʿUbayda is also listed among those who held the first view.]
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: She almost said: "O my son!"
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿رَبَطْنا﴾ is: We made firm and strengthened.
Qatāda said: ﴿لَوْلاۤ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا﴾ i.e. We made her heart firm with faith.
